Lessons.Title: Patterns in the Multiplication Table
ExplanationParagraphs: The source 2021 warm-up shows a complete 5-by-5 multiplication table. Read its cell where one factor's row meets the other factor's column. Both3×5 and5×3 equal15;4×5 and5×4 equal20.

Activity1 Products in the Table uses a SECOND, partially filled 1–10 table with letters at exact ORIGINAL coordinates verified from source SVG pixels. A (row2,column7)=14. B (3,9)=27. C (4,6)=24. D (5,8)=40. E (6,10)=60. F (7,7)=49. G (8,9)=72.

Use commutativity to find A from7×2; add a group of four to move from4×5=20 to4×6=24 for C. Table rows/columns support other strategies. Source pupils then choose THREE MORE empty cells involving factor7, factor9 and factor10; the source does not prescribe the exact three cells.

Activity2 If I Know, Then I Know: Multiplication asks learners to write at least two other related product facts for each starter. Public source example2×4=8 can imply4×2=8,4×4=16 or2×8=16. Other source starters are3×5,4×10,7×2 and5×8. Strategies include switching factors, doubling, adding/taking one group and decomposition, not memorizing property names.

Teacher reviews partner reasoning, MLR2 strategy vocabulary and nonunique responses. The independent Edulytics table is mathematical and source-position aligned, not a copy of original publisher artwork; source Cool-down Find the Missing Product requires login.
These exact source letter values came from the original local SVG image read on the authorized computer. No Stage D/tests/academic approval or publisher graphics copying occurred.

KeyConcepts.Title: Product table lookup
KeyConcepts.Definition: Row and column are factors; their intersection is the product.

KeyConcepts.Title: Commutative property
KeyConcepts.Definition: Switching order of factors keeps product unchanged.

KeyConcepts.Title: One extra group
KeyConcepts.Definition: Advance one column in row n by adding n.

KeyConcepts.Title: Known to unknown
KeyConcepts.Definition: Use a related fact to derive at least two other true products.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use doubles, equal groups or factor rearrangement.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Read a letter from an arbitrary row or column.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Source original A–G have fixed positions visible on the original image.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Map letter to both labelled axes before multiplying.
Use mirrored table cells to justify the same product.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assume three other blanks have unique fixed answer positions.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Original asks students to choose cells with factors7,9 and10.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Teacher checks chosen coordinates and explanations; avoid fake single-answer tasks.
